meta.source_system: BGP-4 peer finite state machine (one FSM as seen by one endpoint for one configured peer), transcribed from RFC 4271 section 8. RFC 4271 is a public standard (Internet Standards Track; the BGP-4 specification).
meta.source_citation: RFC 4271 (January 2006), section 8 'BGP Finite State Machine (FSM)': the event list of sec.8.1.1-8.1.5 (Events 1-28, numbering per sec.8.2.1.4) plus the per-state paragraphs of sec.8.2.2. Per-edge citations with snapshot line ranges in meta.edges_with_citations.
meta.semantics_class: event: the actions are protocol events (sec.8.1's own event names, administrative / timer / TCP / message classes); their names are part of the behavior and do not follow state renamings -- candidate groups in groups/ declare semantics "fixed". The relabel rows in expected.json are the diagnostic contrast reading, not the protocol-true one.
meta.encoding: states 6..7 = unreachable padding (self-loop only); undeclared (state, event) pairs self-loop with reward 0
meta.reward_rule: rewards all zero: the BGP FSM defines no payoff; the reward layer carries no information, all conclusions come from the transition layer

transcription_notes: KEPT (one FSM per connection): the model transcribes ONE endpoint's automaton -- sec.8.2.1: 'BGP MUST maintain a separate FSM for each configured peer' (snapshot txt:2825); the two-peer collision resolution of sec.6.8 is a cross-connection procedure, not a state of one FSM, and the model does not merge two peers into one machine.

KEPT (base-attributes policy): the sec.8.2.2 prose branches on the optional session attributes of sec.8.1.1; the transcription takes the base configuration (DelayOpen=FALSE, PassiveTcpEstablishment=FALSE, DampPeerOscillations=FALSE, SendNOTIFICATIONwithoutOPEN=FALSE, CollisionDetectEstablishedState=FALSE), the parameterization sec.8.2.1.3 itself sketches: 'If an Optional Session attribute cannot be set to TRUE, the events supporting that set of options do not have to be supported' (txt:2885-2895). Events that are separate numbered events (4, 5, 12, 13, 20) are transcribed at their own declared outcomes even though they presuppose an attribute -- the RFC numbers them as events in their own right (sec.8.2.1.4, txt:2923-2928).

NOT COLLECTED (attribute-conditional branches, one per paragraph branch): Connect Events 16/17 DelayOpen=TRUE branch 'stays in the Connect state' (txt:3071-3087); Connect Event 18 DelayOpenTimer-running branch 'changes its state to Active' (txt:3104-3115); Active Events 16/17 DelayOpen=TRUE branch 'stays in the Active state' (txt:3330-3338); Established Events 19/23 CollisionDetectEstablishedState branch (txt:4039-4062) -- base reading: 'Normally, a Detect Collision will be ignored in the Established state' (sec.8.1.5 Event 23 attribute status, txt:2319-2325). Each collected edge's citation names its branch.

NOT COLLECTED (Idle damping group): Events 6, 7 and 13 in Idle -- 'If the DampPeerOscillations attribute is set to TRUE, the following three additional events may occur within the Idle state' ... 'The method of preventing persistent peer oscillation is outside the scope of this document' (txt:2993-3005): no transition is declared, so the pairs collapse to the policy self-loop (reward 0).

NOT COLLECTED (explicit no-change / ignored): Idle Events 2 and 8 'are ignored in the Idle state' (txt:2964-2965) and the Idle catch-all 'Any other event (Events 9-12, 15-28) received in the Idle state does not cause change in the state of the local system' (txt:3007-3008); the start events (Events 1, 3-7) 'are ignored' in Connect (txt:3015), Active (txt:3260), OpenSent (txt:3499-3500), OpenConfirm (txt:3712-3713) and Established (txt:3937-3938). All collapse to the same self-loop as undeclared pairs, per the tcp/http2/ppp encoding policy.

NOT COLLECTED (tracked/ignored, no declared transition): OpenSent Events 14/16/17 'This second TCP connection is tracked per Connection Collision processing (Section 6.8) until an OPEN message is received' (txt:3560-3564) and Event 15 'is ignored' (txt:3566-3567); OpenConfirm Events 14/16/17 'needs to track the second connection' (txt:3784-3787) and Event 15 'will ignore the second connection attempt' (txt:3789-3790); Established Event 14 'will cause the second connection to be tracked' (txt:4019-4020), Event 15 'will be ignored' (txt:4022-4023), Events 16/17 'SHALL be tracked until it sends an OPEN message' (txt:4025-4027). No state-change sentence appears in any of these paragraphs.

NOT COLLECTED (no transition phrase): Established Event 11's paragraph declares actions only -- 'sends a KEEPALIVE message, and restarts its KeepaliveTimer, unless the negotiated HoldTime value is zero' (txt:4007-4013) -- with no state-change sentence, in contrast to OpenConfirm Event 11 which says 'remains in the OpenConfirmed state' (txt:3782). Transcribed as undeclared (policy self-loop).

KEPT (conditional branch, protocol-internal condition): OpenConfirm Event 19's paragraph declares only the collision-drop branch 'changes its state to Idle' (txt:3828-3846); the no-collision case carries no declared transition. The declared branch is transcribed and the condition is named in the edge's citation -- collision handling is core sec.6.8 machinery, not an optional session attribute, so this branch is in base scope.

KEPT (event naming and numbering): event names are sec.8.1's printed names in RFC event-number order; the action index = event number - 1. Event 20 is printed 'BGPOpen with DelayOpenTimer running' (txt:2710) and appears in the model as 'BGPOpen_with_DelayOpenTimer_running'; Event 7's header wraps across two snapshot lines (txt:2490-2491) and the model uses the unwrapped form. The numbering 1-28 is the RFC's own (sec.8.2.1.4, txt:2923-2928).
